concept.name: Breakout
concept.definition: A price move above an established resistance level, range boundary, or chart-pattern upper boundary. In classical chart analysis a breakout is interpreted as evidence that demand has overcome supply at that level; it is an analytical reading, and a meaningful fraction of breakouts fail.
concept.intuition: Price finally escapes the ceiling that had been capping it, suggesting buyers are now willing to pay more than before.
concept.mechanics: Identified when price closes (or trades, depending on convention) above the watched level; confirmation heuristics include expanding volume, follow-through in subsequent sessions, and a successful retest of the broken level as new support.
concept.failure_modes: False breakouts are frequent, especially on low volume; price pokes above the level, draws in breakout buyers, then closes back inside the old range.
concept.misconceptions: That every break of resistance is the start of a new trend; without confirmation, single-bar breaks are routinely reversed.
concept.example: ChartSchool documents WorldCom briefly poking above its 62 range resistance in mid-June 1999 — a breakout that failed within days and was nullified by a gap down.
